children: Li Ming, a 52-year-old Chinese national, has been accused of operating a network of companies smuggling restricted Nvidia
artificial-intelligence chips into China, people familiar with the matter told The Wall Street Journal.

Li was allegedly deeply involved in the activities of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company where Alice Huang, the romantic partner of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, was a managing director. The Journal reports that Li participated in major decisions at Megaspeed and also had a role in other companies trading Nvidia chips.

The operation garnered attention for its alleged efforts to help Chinese companies obtain advanced computing power in violation of U.S. export controls, far beyond the initial Megaspeed scandal that impacted Jensen Huang at Nvidia.

Authorities in Singapore charged Li and others with fraud in February 2025 for allegedly purchasing servers equipped with Nvidia chips and misrepresenting their intended use. Prosecutors claim Li stated the hardware was for his local company, Luxuriate Your Life, but instead it was transshipped to Malaysia and subsequently to an undisclosed third location. Several companies were implicated in the charges, although Megaspeed was not among them.

Li, Alice Huang, and her husband, Kang Wei, have reportedly worked together for years, including establishing a joint venture called Century Longteng in 2021. By January 2023, Li appeared as Century Longteng's chief strategy officer at a Shanghai AI equipment company.

Following the Biden administration's 2021 restrictions on Nvidia semiconductor sales to China, individuals and companies allegedly sought new routes to acquire these chips. Li, Huang, and Kang reportedly established a network of partners in Southeast Asia to supply Chinese clientele. Megaspeed was registered as a Singaporean company and became a member of Nvidia’s cloud partner program in November 2023, after citing Alibaba as an anchor customer. This status allowed it priority access to Nvidia's latest chips.

Sources say Megaspeed initially offered legal offshore computing power to Alibaba in Malaysia, but in violation of U.S. export controls, some servers were sent to Century Litong, a Shanghai tech company. Century Longteng was reportedly a key shareholder of Century Litong until 2024. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on an internal "no sell" list in June 2025 when investigations began in the U.S. and Singapore.

Following Alice Huang's departure from Megaspeed in August 2025, the company diminished its Singaporean operations. However, the group is now said to be operating a new venture called Novagate Cloud, which claims to be an Nvidia cloud partner running data centers with Nvidia Blackwell chips. Shipment records obtained by the Journal reportedly show Novagate received at least $300M in Nvidia hardware in the first five months of 2025 through a Malaysian entity.

While Novagate lists two Singaporeans as its director and secretary, these individuals are also associated with companies related to Century Litong. Several individuals involved have recently faced charges in Singapore for similar crimes. As of now, Li Ming remains out on bail while his criminal case is ongoing.
